hint.spinta: Four goodbyes, then the six o'clock ferry. My mother boards alone, this time.
hint.indizio: Take Livia past those who'll say goodbye, and to the Pier by six in the evening.

merlettaia.margine: One lace to let her go. The others I'll weave alone.

1.1: At six in the evening my mother boarded the ferry. By choice, this time.
1.2: I'll write to you, my Ada. And this time the letters will arrive.

2.1: I waved goodbye from the window. I had no thread to go down to the Pier.
2.2: She turned round three times. At the third, I closed the window.

3.1: Years later, my finest lace hangs in the church, without a name.
3.2: The island children don't know who made it.

4.1: The sun rose every day. Nobody ever knew why.
4.0: Every night, at one minute to six, the lace was finished.

2zeno.1: I waved goodbye from the window. I had no thread to go down to the Pier.
2zeno.2: Zeno carried her suitcase to the ferry. This time she knew where she was going.

3nina.1: Years later, my finest lace hangs in the church, without a name.
3nina.2: Nina, who teaches here, brings her pupils to see it. Nobody knows who made it.

hint.spinta: Livia at the Pier at nine, as in 1951. As Grandmother would want.
hint.indizio: Three hours, three columns: each hour Livia must take one step towards the Pier.

1.1: At nine the lace knotted itself. A single knot, for every thread.
1.2: My mother was at the Pier, as in 1951. The ferry was waiting.

2.1: The bell struck a wrong hour, more out of tune than ever.
2.2: Then the lace undid itself, backwards, all the way to the evening.

3.1: I woke up on yesterday evening, with four notes under the door.
3.2: Grandmother's note was still there, folded in four. I decided not to open it again.

4.1: I have seen this lace before.
4.2: Clotilde's stitch: whoever repeats it, repeats it for ever.

hint.spinta: Move only your own thread. The others follow the plan my mother wrote.
hint.indizio: Stay below: whoever passes over you gives you something. Six people before six p.m.

seppia.margine: I have a coral thread. My mother weaves, I walk.

1.1: My mother took the lace pillow. Her hands already knew it.
1.2: Go, my Ada. The coral thread is yours.

2.1: I have a thread, now. And a life: school, Nina, the mainland.
2.2: In September I took the ferry with Nina. She was laughing; I wasn't.

3.1: Within a year the island had forgotten my mother.
3.2: Then, little by little, I began to forget her too.

4.2: I know because now and then the day is kinder than it should be.

2nina.1: I have a thread, now. And a life: school, Nina, the mainland.
2nina.2: In September Nina was waiting for me at the landing in Venice, books under her arm.

perline.L_teresa: A letter from Ada, for Teresa
perline.L_1951: The 1951 letter, kept by Don Piero, for Ada

hint.spinta: No crossings: plant up to five occasions and let it happen. You can try again.
hint.indizio: Morning bread, afternoon festival, evening lantern: each goes where they please.

aperto.margine: I command no one. I plant an occasion and wait.

1.1: My mother and I pinned only occasions: warm bread at seven,
1.2: the festival in the Square at five, the lantern at eight. They did the rest.

2.1: The threads crossed by themselves, as each one wished. Everyone has a thread.

3.1: The lace pillow stayed in the church, like a relic nobody uses any more.
3.2: The bell in the bell tower, at last, rings in tune.

4.1: For a whole winter I learned to command people.
4.2: Then I learned to know them.

2bepi.1: The threads crossed by themselves, as each one wished. Everyone has a thread.
2bepi.2: Me too. My mother too. Bepi waves to Nina with his good arm.

mancanze.lettere: My mother's letters are still in the well.
mancanze.riconciliate: Teresa and Marta still aren't speaking.

mancanze.memoria: Too many have forgotten my name. I need four people who remember me.
